artifact_note: SAKAMOTO-139 A2 Pixel evidence ledger. It follows the A1 contract artifact shape but records real Android/VpnService/TUN/VPP observations, fixture failures, and evidence-integrity caveats. It does not claim external forwarding.
question: Can a bounded asynchronous UID fact provider attribute real Android IPv4/IPv6 TCP/UDP tuples for controlled App UIDs without blocking FlowOwner, mutating the canonical key, cross-App cache contamination, or doing Android broker/socket/transport work for a dropped UID?
working_assumption: FlowOwner remains selected from the direction-independent canonical tuple. UID is an asynchronous, scoped policy fact; owner turns remain nonblocking and UID never enters the canonical FlowOwner key.

finding_ledger.update: A2 proves narrow Chrome UID 10180 IPv4 TCP/UDP attribution, long-window and near-simultaneous two-ordinary-App IPv4 TCP/UDP observations (Chrome 10180 plus Maps 10176), a historical one-off exact-target IPv6 UID completion plus final IPv6 tuple/proc observations with intermittent target uid=-1, live Java contract replay rejection at the tun/VPP boundary, and a fresh UID-drop protect-broker boundary with zero requests/completions/failures. A1 proves the cross-implementation replay/cache/key baseline; the Android control does not prove native VPP owner/cache invariance. A2 does not prove the full IPv4/IPv6 TCP/UDP matrix, reverse closure, lifecycle closure, repeatable IPv6 acceptance, or per-dropped-packet socket/transport zero.

finding_ledger.update: Decisive fixture failure: local socket was Wi-Fi 192.168.4.151; RuntimeService was not active. This is recorded as an A2 evidence gap, not an architecture interruption.
Plugin selection, explicit sentinel, and comma-separated dual allow-list corrections were applied and their post-correction raw evidence is retained.

supported_claim: A controlled ordinary App UID (Chrome 10180) produced real IPv4 TCP and UDP tuples entering tun0/VPP owner resolution and reaching the post-policy shim boundary.

Chrome produced real IPv6 TCP target tuples at the VPP post-policy shim boundary and /proc/net/tcp6 carried UID 10180; one historical exact-target 443 resolver completion reported uid=10180, while final HTTP/80 and ULA retries remained uid=-1 for the exact target.

Narrow long-window and near-simultaneous two-ordinary-App IPv4 TCP/UDP observations saw Chrome UID 10180 and Maps UID 10176 on the same allowed tun0; resolver completions retained Chrome/Maps UIDs and VPP shim output remained nonzero.

The bounded Android contract emitted miss, coalescing, completion, cache hit/eviction, refresh, unavailable, package-scoped wrong-UID rejection, and live replay outcomes with pending/cache high-water bounded at four and flow-id high-water bounded at eight.

A1 Host/model and the rebuilt Android Java control reject wrong-owner, wrong-generation, duplicate, stale, wrong-scope, wrong-UID, cross-App cache-hit, and FlowOwner-key mutation replays; the Android control does not prove native VPP owner/cache invariance.
The corrected owner-resolver plugin selection and dual allow-list harness are ordinary POC corrections, not changes to owner-inline/nonblocking/FlowOwner invariants.
A historical narrow UID 12628 IPv4 UDP observation exists, but its original immutable raw was overwritten by a later run and must be treated with that provenance caveat.

A fresh dedicated Chrome UID 10180 drop run observed uid-block=6/6438 and no protect-broker request/completion/failure; this is a broker-boundary observation only, not a general socket/transport-zero proof.
non_claims: No complete A2 acceptance across the required two-App IPv4/IPv6 TCP/UDP, reverse, concurrent, refresh, and drop matrix; the two-App IPv4 TCP/UDP and concurrent observations remain narrow PASS only.

The Android replay control exercises live Java pending/cache state, but it is not an independent proof that native VPP owner/cache state was unchanged; A1 Host/model remains the cross-implementation baseline.
No repeatable IPv6 target completion at the VPP post-policy boundary; one historical exact-target completion is intermittent and not reproduced by final retries.
No complete current-UID IPv4 drop proof with independent per-dropped-packet zero socket/transport counters; the fresh run only proves a narrow zero protect-broker boundary.
No Android ConnectivityManager/OEM-general timing claim beyond the Pixel run.
No reverse-traffic acceptance claim; the concurrent-distinct-tuple observation is narrow and does not prove the full matrix.
Android live Java replay assertions are not an independent proof that native VPP live owner/cache state was unchanged; the Java seam must not be treated as a native invariance proof.
No external SOCKS/HTTP forwarding, reverse forwarding, lwIP external transport, or B1 full VPP claim.
No production readiness, queue/cache capacity, multi-user, persistence, or OEM compatibility claim.
